subject: Committed GPU runway & isolation: post-call checklist
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@helixbio.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Committed GPU runway & isolation: post-call checklist

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we stay aligned heading into your procurement window. I kept this intentionally short.

Key pain points you emphasized:
- Unpredictable inference cost spikes during weekly batch jobs (up to 3x).
- Need for tenant-level isolation for PHI models (auditability + network controls).
- Latency degradation under concurrency peaks; target is 99th <= 200ms for gen workloads.

Goals you shared:
- Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) with hard isolation and optional burst capacity.
- Predictable monthly spend for FY28 planning; procurement decision by end of May.
- Proof-of-concept in dev region for 2 weeks before committing to annual contract.

What we propose (high level):
1) Dedicated pool: 8 x A100/80GB equivalent reserved; isolated VPC + KMS integration.
2) Burst policy: allow up to +25% temporary burst from shared capacity for non-PHI workloads.
3) SLOs: p95 latency target 120ms, p99 290ms; availability SLA 99.9% for reserved pool.
4) Onboarding: 2-week canary in your dev VPC -> run sample traffic and smoke tests -> sign-off for production cutover.

Immediate next steps I’m proposing (actionable):
- We’ll send a short proposal with two pricing bands (standard reserved vs reserved+isolation) by Thu (5/6). [Ben will draft]
- Helix to confirm PO timeline and a shortlist of 3 representative workloads for the POC by Friday (5/7).
- Technical kickoff (30m) when you’re ready; Jordan to lead the ops runbook.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sla-options-helix-v1.pdf (pricing + SLA options), isolation-architecture-sketch.png (high-level VPC/KMS flow).

If that aligns, I’ll flag Ben to put numbers together and Jordan to prepare the onboarding checklist.

Thanks,

Lukas Meyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lukas.meyer@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

--
Redwood Inference | Developer-first LLM inference
From: Emma Li <emma.li@helixbio.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Committed GPU runway & isolation: post-call checklist

Lukas —

Appreciate the concise summary. All of this matches what we discussed. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The PHI workloads must run in an environment that restricts egress by default (we need explicit allow rules).
- For the POC, we’ll include both a small-batch retrain pipeline and a live scoring endpoint (to test KV cache behavior).
- Procurement: internal target is to have a PO signed by 5/28, but we may need a 2–3 week extension if legal requests redlines.

We’ll confirm the three workloads by EOD Friday. Also, can you include an optional line for SOC2 compliance evidence collection cadence? Our security team usually asks about quarterly evidence for the first year.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Li
Director of Infrastructure, Helix Bio
emma.li@helixbio.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@helixbio.ai>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Committed GPU runway & isolation: post-call checklist

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the clarifications. A few follow-ups from the commercial/ops side so we can size the proposal correctly:

1) Expected steady-state QPS for the scoring endpoint and peak concurrent sessions (helpful to size cluster and KV cache).
2) Data residency preference (we have US-east and US-west private nodes) — you mentioned US but let us know region preference.
3) If you need monthly metering exports beyond the console (CSV or S3 delivery) put that in your note; there is a modest add-on for daily S3 dumps.

Proposed timeline: draft proposal Thu (5/6) -> POC kickoff week of 5/10 -> 2-week POC (5/10–5/24) -> procurement sign-off target 5/28. If legal needs extra time, we can offer a short-term month-to-month pilot pricing for June to avoid a hard stop.

SLA options attached include the isolation add-on we discussed; SOC2 evidence cadence is captured on page 3.

Action items for Helix (please reply inline):
- Workloads + expected QPS: [Helix reply]
- Region preference: [Helix reply]
- Security evidence cadence requirement: [Helix reply]

I’ll aim to include two commercial options in the deck: Reserved (lower commitment, lower price) and Reserved+Isolation (higher commitment, includes dedicated KMS + VPC isolation).

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Emma Li <emma.li@helixbio.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Committed GPU runway & isolation: post-call checklist

Ben / Lukas —

Thanks — answering inline below: 

- Workloads/QPS: Scoring endpoint steady-state ~120 QPS, bursts to ~420 QPS during lab reporting windows. Batch retrain: ~12 jobs/week, each job runs for ~90–120 minutes and spikes GPU usage.
- Region: US-west preferred (Latency to our services matters).
- Security cadence: Quarterly evidence for the first 12 months; SOC2 summary + audit log extracts will suffice for initial review.

We confirmed the three workloads internally and will share the test payloads by Friday. 5/28 PO target is accurate; we’ll flag legal now to reduce redline time. If you can include month-to-month pilot pricing as a fall-back, that would be helpful.

Appreciate the speedy turn. Looking forward to the proposal.

Emma
